chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Hamza, who said:

I sought permission to enter upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), so he came out to me and his lips were moving. So I told him. He said: 'Did you realize that, O Thumali?' I said: 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' He said: 'By Allah, I spoke a speech that no one ever spoke, except that Allah would suffice him for what worries him from the affairs of his world and his Hereafter.'
He said: I said to him, 'Inform me of it.' He said: 'Yes. The one who says when he exits from his house.'

'In the Name of Allah, Allah suffices me. I rely upon Allah. O Allah, I ask You for the goodness of all my affairs, and I seek refuge with You from the disgrace of the world and the punishment of the Hereafter.' Allah will suffice him for what worries him from the affairs of his world and his Hereafter.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite when leaving the house for protection from worldly worries?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) disclosed a unique supplication to Thumamah, emphasizing its efficacy in divinely sufficing the believer from worldly and religious anxieties. This narration, recorded in al-Kafi, highlights the spiritual protection granted through the specific invocation of 'Hasbunallah' and trust in Allah upon leaving one's home, reinforcing the Shia tradition of integrating daily actions with divine remembrance.
